title: CompletionPacket
description: Versioned return contract (FR-3) for any role reporting back to a coordinator, runtime-neutral. Contract version completion-packet.v1. Formalises the verdict block already produced informally by the Claude Code builder agent (.claude/agents/builder.md) — Verdict/Files changed/Spec sections/What was implemented/Plan gap/G1 attempts/Notes for caller/DID NOT TOUCH.
$comment: status enum is exactly the builder verdict set (SUCCESS, PLAN_GAP, G1_FAILED) — no drift permitted; any new terminal a Builder can return requires a coordinated schema bump. commit_sha is nullable because a PLAN_GAP or G1_FAILED result, or a SUCCESS awaiting a coordinator-owned commit, has no commit yet.

executionPolicy.description: The execution policy in force during a run, normalized per references/execution-policy.md. Structurally the work packet's execution_policy PLUS allowed_files: the effective policy folds in the work packet's top-level allowed_files so the object is self-contained and evaluable without the original packet. Semantics are conjunctive — a path is writable iff it matches allowed_files (when present) AND write_scope (when present) AND no protected_paths entry.
executionPolicy.$comment: Every key except allowed_files is duplicated from work-packet.schema.json properties.execution_policy, because validate-packet.mjs compiles each packet schema standalone with no addSchema, so a cross-file $ref would fail to resolve, be swallowed by the compile try/catch, and silently degrade that packet to the structural floor. validate-packet.test.mjs asserts every shared key stays identical and that allowed_files is the only permitted divergence.

allowed_files.description: Folded copy of the work packet's top-level allowed_files, normalized. Conjunctive with write_scope.

write_scope.description: Repo-relative glob patterns this dispatch may write. Conjunctive with allowed_files: a path must match BOTH when both are present. An empty array means nothing is writable.

protected_paths.description: Repo-relative glob patterns that must never be written, overriding allowed_files and write_scope.

egress_allowlist.description: Permitted egress hosts. Only meaningful with network_egress: allowlist.

deploy_authority.description: The only expressible value is false. A policy can withhold deploy authority but can never confer it; deployment stays operator-owned.

expires_at.description: Instant after which this policy must not be honoured. Expiry is evaluated at dispatch time by the coordinator, not by this schema.

packet_id.description: Echoes the packet_id of the work-packet.v1 this result answers.

summary.description: Concise operator-facing summary of what was done.

effective_policy.description: The policy actually in force during this run. Echoed so a coordinator can detect divergence between what was dispatched and what the executing runtime believed it was bound by.

effective_policy_hash.description: Lowercase SHA-256 over the canonical serialization of the normalized policy DECLARATIONS (never a resolved file set), computed by normalizeExecutionPolicy in scripts/packet-contract/execution-policyPure.mjs. Declaration-level so a coordinator can recompute it from the work packet alone.

policy_evaluation.description: Whether policy compliance was actually assessed. Distinguishes 'checked, clean' from 'never checked' — an empty policy_violations array cannot. Absence must be read as not_evaluated.

policy_violations.description: Policy violations observed during the run. Only meaningful when policy_evaluation is violated.

documentation_impact.description: Diataxis class of documentation this change affects. Advisory: no gate consumes it yet. Absence means the producer did not classify, which is NOT the same as none.

changed_docs.description: Documentation files this change touched. Must be a subset of changed_files.

doc_exemption_reason.description: Why no documentation changed despite code changing. Required by producer convention when documentation_impact is none and changed_files contains non-doc code; see .claude/agents/builder.md.

release_evidence.description: Post-completion evidence linking this packet to what was deployed and observed. No tested-commit field: the top-level commit_sha already carries it.
release_evidence.$comment: A SUCCESS completion MAY carry canary_result: fail. Canaries run after the work completes, so attaching the observation must not force a status rewrite; the consuming release gate decides what a failed canary means.
